Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The bug report indicates an issue with selecting namespaced attributes using a wildcard in the expression, specifically "xml/@*". The test fails because the selection returns null, but using a namespace-prefixed attribute wildcard like "@x:*" works correctly. The suggested fix points to an if condition in a DOMAttributeIterator method, which is likely the testAttr method given the line numbers and logic.

Examining the testAttr(Attr) method:
- It retrieves the prefix and local name of the attribute node.
- It excludes namespace declaration attributes ("xmlns").
- It then checks if the local name of the attribute matches the name requested or if a wildcard "*" is used.
- Next, it compares the prefix of the test attribute (testPrefix) with the attribute node's prefix (nodePrefix).
- The current implementation returns true only if these prefixes exactly match (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)).
- If they do not match, it tries to compare their namespaces instead by resolving them via parent.getNamespaceURI(prefix).

The problem is the condition at line 84:
```java
if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) {
    return true;
}
```
This rejects cases where the testPrefix is null but the nodePrefix has some namespace prefix, or vice versa. In particular, if the expression is "@*", the testPrefix is null, but nodePrefix may be non-null, so this condition returns false, leading to failure to select namespaced attributes when using the wildcard.

The proposed fix is to loosen this condition to accept matches if testPrefix is null (as happens with '@*'), regardless of the nodePrefix:
```java
if (testPrefix == null || equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) {
    return true;
}
```
This will enable attributes with any prefix (i.e., namespaced attributes) to be matched by a wildcard testLocalName of "*".

This diagnosis aligns with the failing test of namespaced attributes and the bug report's suggestion. The faulty logic is in the DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr method checking prefixes too strictly for wildcards.

Hence, the bug occurs because when the attribute name is wildcard '*', the code only matches attributes whose prefix is equal to the (null) testPrefix, which excludes namespaced attributes with a prefix. The fix is to also allow prefix mismatch when testPrefix is null (wildcard).
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr(org.w3c.dom.Attr)
